column5: regmove will not tie an AND to a parameter copy unless the next insn sets it again: mask and shift the parameter in place (flags &= m; flags >>= 12), then a separate priority = flags - 1.
A chain of early returns (if (!p) return 0; ...) with one object = input copy read only by the last test keeps both pointer registers; nested ifs and && chains let cse merge them.
The graphic index is narrowed in the call: (u16)(entry->graphic + 0x121); the truncation that combine later proves redundant keeps the constant load and copy apart from the byte.

A plain for loop that indexes a parts base pointer declared in the body (parts[i]) plus an inline SetAction(state, 1, 5) helper gives the hoisted constants and giv order; the hand-rotated pointer walk needed the pin.

Same indexed for loop; the queue-part step is an inline helper whose body is the shared ARMOR_QUEUE_PART_ACTION statement macro, which doubles the count pointer refs (the r3/r4 order) and leaves the dead zero pseudo that owns r8.

cse (fold_rtx) always moves a register with a known constant second, so the ROM order base+offset needs the base set outside the add's cse block (cse stops at a NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END, i.e. a statement macro around the base setup); no shared macro is evident for it.
A two-case switch written case 23 then case 10 gives the ROM's layout, and a second manager view pointer read only in the case 10 arm (reached through a label) keeps the early r1-to-r3 copy.
Two plain for loops over one index; the byte is updated in place with two compound assignments (buffer[i] ^= word; buffer[i] &= mask), which loop.c turns into the pointer walk and countdown itself.
Plain field code: p->flags88 |= 2; p->flags88 &= ~1; as two statements (README fact 103) gives the or-with-zero, and the literal 1 is shared by cse; no named constants needed.
Field code with no locals: if (++particle->frame > 15), offsetY += velocityY, and the phase test read from particle->frame again; cse supplies the registers the pins forced.

Second-pointer cause (as Hresvelgr_PlayDescent): the shake is an inline called in both branches (HasFlags, then the hit-flag test) and jump2 merges the two copies; that makes cse's first path from entry reach the tail, so the tail's copy of p becomes the parameter register and the early code the swapped copy. No pin.
One slot variable carries the next window, then its previous-link address, then the window's own previous slot after the join; with separate variables the allocator puts next in r1.

Without the r0 pin the sample and the coordinate swap r0/r2: local-alloc ranks the coordinate quantity (12 refs) above the sample (8 refs) in every ordinary form tried (types, operand order, shared or per-block variables).

Plain for loop over slots[i] with the first slot's flags test kept as written and an inline helper for the delay and flag stores; the pins were holding three hand-made pointers that loop creates by itself.

The removed test is a u8 hasFlag(segment, u8 mask) helper behind isRemoved: its byte conversions add three RTL insns to the loop (40 at the second loop pass), so the activeCount address (threshold 13 * life 3 = 39) stays under loop.c's move test and is recomputed each iteration (cause group: loop.c size threshold, helper types decide insn count).

One function-scope id variable shared by all three cases (the index in case 0, the category*6+index result in cases 1 and 2) with block-local category and index; the shared pseudo is what blocks r1/r2 and pushes menu and pending to r3/r4.

All but one insn fall out of plain code (pressed = MASK; pressed &= keys); the first test needs RTL (and one keys) with the 1 not known constant to cse, which swaps it in every ordinary form (shared variable, types, loop wrappers).

Plain early returns, a for loop and bitfield stores match once the slot is read from the trigger again after the inline status test and before the branch (comma expression); the pin and barriers were forcing those two copies.

Second-pointer cause: the body is an inline that returns early (if above the floor return 0) and the caller keeps a typed copy of p for the last call; cse reruns the first block per path with stale last-use data, so the copy stays for the inline and p for the tail. No barrier.

Plain do-while with five mask locals before the loop and nested tests gets the shape, but four allocation details stay off (flags copy to r4 before the first branch, state address kept in r1, 120 not hoisted, zero in r1); each needs its own lever and no ordinary form covered all.

Plain if/else with inline helpers; the status helper returns u8 through two returns, whose zero-extension keeps jump from threading the status==0 path (what the barrier forced), and show/hide written in each branch cross-jump on their own.

Plain field code with volatile frame/interval fields and a u16 frame local gets every instruction; five pool-constant offset loads take other registers (r3/r1 where the draft has r0/r1/r2), a reload spill-rotation difference that one rotation shift does not explain.
The loop reads the saved id from the game state twice (test, then argument) with no local; the pins were holding a hand-built row pointer and id register.

Literal `& 31` masks (HImode for the shifted components) let loop hoist both masks and give the ROM registers with no pin, but the red AND then ties to the color instead of a copy of the mask (4 insns); the mask-first order needs a mask cse cannot see as constant.

The dead abs code is four identical-call arms (`if (ax > az) { if (x > 0) F; else F; } else if (z > 0) F; else F;`) merged by jump2 after flow, which gives the ROM registers with no barrier; three arms merge but the last arm call falls into the join label, gets flow (use 0) nop and stays apart (12 extra insns).

An inline that reads actor->direction and writes variant/mirror through pointers, plus a u8 local for mirror | entry->flags (its extra zero-extend flips combine's operand swap back and keeps the two byte loads as QI pseudos), replaces both pins.

Two inlines as in the matched Golem sibling: the direction helper writing variant and mirror through pointers, then the select helper called with (entry->value, variant, mirror | entry->flags); the earlier attempt had the operands of the OR the other way round, which is what moved the mirror pointer.
The dead movs r7,#0 is a zero flag operand ORed into child->flags inside the loop: set before the loop, it survives flow and combine folds its use afterwards (scope fact 94), so no r7 pin is needed.
Same child-callback loop as Actor_UpdateBlinkBurstDisappearance: a zero flag operand in the loop replaces the r7 pin.

Reload's spill rotation was one step off: the first random draw indexes the table at its literal address (RANDOM_TABLE_ADDR), so reload loads that constant and the later ldrsh index lands in r2 with no r1 pin.

local-alloc: the callback address is a block-local qty with r0 free over its two-insn life, so it takes r0; the ROM's r1 needs r0 held across the store by another local (or the callback global with an r0 conflict) and nothing in the ROM shows one. Ruled out: reload (the rotation r0,r2,r3,r5 leaves no slot for it), update_equiv_regs moving an early set (a pool-loaded symbol never qualifies), callback set earlier or per arm, the sibling SetPlayback inline, field/slot/void* forms, s16 wait, -1/65535. MessageWindow_ShowMessage's second arm shows the same r1 where the address is born after the callback and takes r0; here the address is the per-arm pointer in r4, so the missing piece is whatever short local the original had between the load and the store. The unit keeps a private copy of struct MessageWindow (include/message_window.h); porting it to the header struct is still untried.

global-alloc liveness: 0x2f0 (the action offset, reused by cse as the case 2 collision mask) must be live through case 1 so the shared 0x3FF mask takes ip instead of sl; the barrier at the end supplies that use and no natural later use of the value was found.

local-alloc's three-quantity sort compares by index and misorders the block; a block-local display pointer in the else branch makes a fourth quantity, qsort then orders by priority and the plain flags |= 1 gets the ROM registers with no pin (the capture macro goes too).

The r6 copy is the function's scratch int (the one that holds the MOJISE compare result) loaded with the label name for the GARIGARIKUN and FUTARI compares and reset before PLAYER: cse keeps a copy only when its variable has a later reference than the source's last use, and PLAYER keeps r4 only because the reset ends the equivalence. Bytes match with no counted concession, but the reset is a dead store, so the original wording is still a guess (cause group: second-register copy, cse class head).

The shared zero is a variable assigned 0 in both clamp arms (jump2 merges the two loads into the one at the join, and cse cannot see it as a constant past the join, so the later stores keep it and pendingFlag loads its own); the count store goes through a u8 pointer so it makes no mask zero first, and a dead count < 0 test before the clamp leaves a label that stops reload_cse deleting the first arm's load. No counted concession, but the dead test and per-arm zero are forms found by reading the passes, not known original wording (cause group: zero sharing in byte stores).

The first/second/dest pointer variables were the compiler's own PRE temporaries: written as plain array code (total = owner->pending[index]; total += target->count; ... a = owner->current[index]; b = owner->pending[index]) gcse places the two base addresses as in the ROM; the leftover is min(value, 0) as in QueueLocalItem.
A u8 result local for the masked flag byte adds two insns to contactFlags' live range, so owner outranks it in global alloc and takes sb without the pin.

Each switch case starts with p = actor into one function-scope pointer and uses p: cse keeps p canonical (it outlives actor past the path end), so the second SetFlags address is (p + 0x9c), a different expression to gcse PRE than the first (actor + 0x9c), and actor dies at each copy so both share r5 (cause group: gcse PRE kept apart by a second pointer variable tied to the same register).

The probe loops are for loops with the hit tail written out in the body and again after the loop: the for loop's entry-test edge into the code after the loop keeps gcse PRE and cse2 off the second width load, which then inherits the reloaded map address (cause group: loop form decides PRE/cse reach).

jump2 cross-jump: the three Anim_SetSequence tails (pad1 5/6/7) share 'movs r3,#0; bl' and all jump to the fall-through's 'saved = a', but the ROM keeps them whole; own 'saved = a' copies per tail only stay apart if no label stands before the fall-through's copy while flow still puts its (use 0) nop after the default call, and I found no C with both.

combine nonzero-bits: the ROM copies the top g->type byte from a temporary into the long-lived type register and keeps the lsls/lsrs re-extension at the later test, which needs a set of that register whose upper bits combine cannot prove zero; plain reads (with or without gcse PRE of the QI load) and u8 inline getters all let combine drop the extension, so the operand barrier stays.

cse1 class head: a function-level mask variable shared by the count==0 site and the last setFlags outlives the cse block, so make_regs_eqv keeps it as its own register instead of merging it with the earlier stack-argument 1 (which had left both to reload).

cse1 class head again: the stack argument's 0 is one variable assigned in the argument at both call sites (loop = 0), so it outlives the cse block and is not replaced by the tested allowTurn register that cse knows is 0; the assignment-in-argument form is unusual C and worth a phase-4 look.

local-alloc register choice: the ROM computes the CpuFastSet source (gPaletteBankData + key*32) into r3 with offset in r0 and base in r1, then copies it to r0 after the second argument; every unpinned form ties the sum to r0 through the argument copy (or would take r2), and nothing visible in the ROM occupies r2 there.

Cause group reload round-robin (same as ResourceStation_CheckInteraction): the early exit was a goto into the final tail; written out as its own Player_InitVisualResources(p); p->savedSpriteResource = -1; return it adds the missing reload choice, jump2 merges the copy away, and the pins, barriers and the pinned EquipmentSlot helper all go (plain i == override->slot)

global-alloc priority: hit (4 refs, life 29) ranks one insn below the flags pointer (4 refs, life 28) and they swap r5/r6; plain field access gives the same PRE register, no C found that shortens hit or lengthens the pointer without moving code

Cause group reload round-robin (same as ResourceStation_CheckInteraction): case 0's slot < 0 failure was a goto into case 2's tail; written out as its own finished = 1; return (as in the activation block) it adds the missing reload choice, jump2 merges it away, and case 1 becomes a plain p->sequence = 2

The merged count stays live past the clamp because the leftover written to the queued slot is min(count, 0) (clear = 0; if (count < 0) clear = count), which also keeps that zero apart from the flag's; second block as UpdateItemMerge (zero per clamp arm, count stored through a pointer).

gcse merged the two actor+0x50 addresses; a second pointer (self = actor before the inlined height lookup, actor = self after its one use) gives the arm its own pseudo, and taking the player position pointer first makes both land in r7 so the copies vanish

the two group lookups were written through a shared goto tail with function-level temporaries; writing the lookup out in each arm with block locals lets jump2 merge the tails itself and the registers fall out

the loop was hand-reduced (pointer locals stepped by a shared constant, a frame struct to force stack slots); an indexed for loop over body->segments[i] with plain spilled locals lets loop.c make the three induction registers itself, and the duration fallback written as a plain = 1 uses the function-wide constant-1 pseudo, which supplies the missing reload choice
same rewrite as ResetDirectionalAnimations: indexed for loop over body->segments[i], plain spilled locals, plain duration = 1
already clean after merging main (the ZeroFill8/CpuFill32 helper change there removed its helper concession); no change from this branch

global-alloc priority: the ROM gives point r4, yAddress r5 and the cell index r6, but cell (4 refs, life 24) outranks both pointers so it takes r4; sharing one temporary between cell and the later zero fixes r4/r5/r6 but takes zero out of local-alloc's block and permutes r8/sb/sl. Same prologue as InteractionMarker and SavedPositionMarker InitializeFromScript

the z store after the 'p' if/else left its mask zero (agbcc expands a field store as (old & 0) | value) in the cse block that reaches the later known-zero stores, so cse rewrote them to that register; storing z inside each arm (jump2 merges the tails) keeps the zero out of that block and the pins and barriers go

global-alloc priority: the ROM hands out the first new high register (r8) to object, then w (sb), then i (sl); in every plain form w (6 refs, life 43) and i (17 refs, life 246) outrank object (12 refs, life 204) so object gets sl. Indexing object->registration[i] in a for loop compiles to the same code as the hand-stepped pointer, so the loop shape is not the cause

The only pin left is the gRandomTable pointer in Item_NextRandom. Loaded first in its block (as the ROM does) it is a local-alloc register in r6 with 3 refs / life 21 per site, but update_equiv_regs (local-alloc.c) doubles the life of a register set once to a constant, so r6 scores 6/84 against 13/164 for the PRE register of &p->drawing and global.c find_reg evicts it (tmp1 < tmp2). Loaded at first use it matches except for that load's position. Tried: param, union view, pointer-sum and single-expression forms, signed %4, a shared table variable, folded sign tests to split the block; none keeps r6. Open: what keeps the ROM's load first without the doubling (a second tied register in r6, or fewer references on the PRE register).

the macros hid a union that made the mask and cell cursor one pseudo; the ROM is an indexed loop whose counter variable is reused by the next loop and whose direction step is written out before each continue, so cse shares one constant 3, loop.c hoists it and jump2 merges the copies

global-alloc order and cse sharing: with the eleven do-while(0) macros written out plainly 31 hunks differ; the ROM keeps zero, then 1, then gRandomTable in r4 and reuses the 0x2B3 address register for flags2CC (adds r2,#0x19), which the draft only gets by sharing one workValue variable and fencing each store

loop.c giv grouping then global-alloc order: the ROM reduces three address givs (flags in sb, position in r7 with a copy in r6 for the inlined height helper, position.y stores in r5 as their own giv); plain indexed C gets the three givs but lets the y group absorb the z read, so the position giv loses priority and the registers permute (39 insns); 130 access-form variants tried

global-alloc order of a dead constant: the 0x0403B714 origin load survives because combine folds its only uses and leaves a (use) insn; unpinned it is allocated last (3 refs) and takes r5, pushing angle to r3 and speed to r4, while the ROM gives it r3 first; needs the origin pseudo to outrank angle (about 8 refs over a 36-insn life) without cse folding its in-arm uses

reload spill order: ten gcse address pseudos are spilled and the ROM's stack-slot order (0x4c,0x48,0x44,0x40,...) follows the order reload evicts them; dropping only the operand barrier in the first block already permutes all ten slots (20 insns), every instruction otherwise identical

Mechanism found, wording not: a plain rewrite (field reads, ++stateFrame, no pointer locals; build/w/N_bounce.c) matches everywhere except that cse1 shares the &stateFrame address across the three late tests (it skips AROUND the shake block and the ring-effect call), so the pointer has 4 refs and global.c's takeover (4/41 > 3/40) evicts the random-table local from r6. In the ROM cse1 stops after each shake statement and at the end of that block: the pointer is then gcse's copy with 3 refs (3/41 < 3/40, no takeover, it falls to r8), reload spills the table to ip through r6, and 0x37E/0x382 are separate constants. Fencing each shake statement with a loop note proves it (5 insns left, only because loop depth doubles the address pseudo's weight), so the original has a label there that folds away after cse1's path scan; inline guards on constant arguments fold too early, unsigned clamps do not fold. Same cause as sub_080399F4 (table local evicted from r6 by a gcse register).

Both counters are clamped on two sides (if (count > 9999) count = 9999; else if (count < 0) count = 0;): combine folds the lower arm away because the value is a halfword plus one, but its label ends cse's path at the join, which is why the ROM reloads 9999 and the gSessionState address after each clamp. Plain gSessionState code otherwise; no address variables.

the random-table read is an inline returning u16 whose low byte the caller takes ((u8)Random()): the halfword load and the truncation are separate insns until combine narrows them to ldrb, which lengthens the animated pointer's life by two insns so the loop counter outranks it for r6; with that a plain for loop with i + 1 written in the argument matches, no pins or barriers

the link-value inline returns u16 (a byte member widened by its return type): its result is then a narrower pseudo that the caller extends into a block-local in r0, so the old fraction is the local evicted from r3 by the loop counter and reloaded into r4; with that the plain for loop and += statements match, no gotos or pointer temporaries

Cause group reload round-robin: scope why showed the ROM made one more reload choice before the not-active arm; the out-of-range test writes its own nearby = 0 and returns, a copy jump2 later merges whole into the final one but whose scratch choice still advances the rotation (README fact 59)

Rewrote from the ROM as a plain for loop over gPlayerCount with two small vector inlines and named path fields; the count copy is loop.c hoisting the global load, and holding category in a local shortens bestDifference's live range by two insns so it outranks the player-slot giv for r6/r7

The occupied test is an inline taking &manager->occupiedMask at the call site (reg+reg address that loop.c hoists and merges with the release statement's; an inline taking manager folds the constant and gcse hoists a second pointer), manager is re-read from the global after the null test, and the slot id is an s8 local.

The x/z scatter keeps its value chain in temporaries (an inline returning value - 127 + *sample through a fresh local, so nothing narrows to HImode and local-alloc ties load, subtract, add and truncation), the index is updated in place (index++; index &= 1023, one death, so it stays a local-alloc quantity) and the sample address is taken before the coordinate is read.

Two causes: (1) pixelX/pixelY written x + p->x[layer] give x and y a copy preference for r5/r4, so find_reg's pass 0 keeps p out of them and p lands in r6; (2) the random table outranks the index pointer only with 6 refs, which the shared header's two helpers give (first sample ParticleRandom_ReadDirectSample, both target samples ParticleRandom_ReadSample, whose read sits in loop notes and counts double), as in sub_080A34BC.

Rewritten from the ROM as plain C: separate digits[4] and screen locals, the projection as the same pointer-taking inline DamageNumber_ProjectPosition uses, and ordinary for loops indexing station->digits[i]; the nine pins were holding a hand-lowered loop in place.
